primary_activity.atb: ATB (All Terrain Biking) — Gravel, Cyclocross, etc.

motors.operating_modes.e_vehicle_classif.evc/au/power-assisted-pedal-cycle: AU Power-Assisted Pedal Cycle, up to 200 W

evc/ca/power-assisted-bicycle.name: Canadian Power-Assisted Bicycle
evc/ca/power-assisted-bicycle.description: Canada's federal e-bike definition, which the provinces built their e-bike laws on: a pedal bicycle on no more than three wheels with electric motors totalling 500 W or less that stop assisting at 32 km/h.

restrictions.rule: Steering handlebars, pedals, no more than three wheels, and capable of being propelled by muscular power
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: One or more electric motors with a total continuous power output rating, measured at the shaft, of 500 W or less
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Assistance engaged by pedalling stops as soon as pedalling stops; assistance engaged by a throttle stops as soon as the brakes are applied
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: The motor can't provide further assistance once the bicycle reaches 32 km/h on level ground
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Needed a motor on/off switch separate from the throttle, or a mechanism that keeps the motor from engaging below 3 km/h
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Needed a label permanently affixed by the manufacturer stating, in English and French, that it is a power-assisted bicycle
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Excluded from the federal motorcycle definition, so no Canada Motor Vehicle Safety Standard ever applied to it
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Repealed from the Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations on February 4, 2021: there's no longer a federal e-bike definition or label
Transport Canada no longer assesses e-bikes against it
Provincial laws such as Ontario's Highway Traffic Act still define their e-bikes by reference to it
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: At import, Transport Canada treats a pedal bicycle with motor assist unable to exceed 32 km/h as non-regulated, assesses one built like a scooter, motorcycle or motor tricycle as that class whatever its speed, and treats a faster one with off-road characteristics as a restricted-use vehicle
Where e-bikes may be ridden is left to provincial, territorial and local governments
In national parks, Parks Canada allows only pedal-assist e-bikes meeting this definition, on designated bike trails at select parks; e-bikes with a throttle may be ridden only on roads

evc/moped.name: Moped, up to 2 hp and 30 mph
evc/moped.description: The moped the classifications naming this group share: a motor of no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) that can't propel it faster than 30 mph. A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it, and each of those holds its own jurisdiction's license, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules.

restrictions.rule: Its motor produces no more than 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W)
restrictions.citation: Revised Code of Washington §46.04.304; Utah Code §41-6a-102; West Virginia Code §17C-1-5a

restrictions.rule: The motor can't propel it faster than 30 mph
restrictions.citation: Revised Code of Washington §46.04.304; Utah Code §41-6a-102; West Virginia Code §17C-1-5a

restrictions.rule: Past its jurisdiction's e-bike limits; one within them is an electric bicycle instead

evc/motor-driven-cycle.name: Motor-Driven Cycle, up to 5 hp
evc/motor-driven-cycle.description: The motor-driven cycle the classifications naming this group share: a motorcycle whose motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W). A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it, and each of those holds its own jurisdiction's license, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels
Its motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W)
Past its jurisdiction's e-bike limits, and its moped's where the jurisdiction has one
restrictions.citation: Revised Code of Washington §46.04.332; Wyoming Statutes §31-5-102(a)(xxiii)

evc/motorcycle.name: Motorcycle, over 5 hp
evc/motorcycle.description: A road motorcycle whose motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W), which is a motorcycle under every classification naming this group. A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it, and each of those holds its own jurisdiction's license, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels
Its motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W)
Built for highway use; one built for off-highway use is an off-highway motorcycle instead

evc/off-highway-motorcycle.name: Off-Highway Motorcycle
evc/off-highway-motorcycle.description: An electric motorcycle built for off-highway use, such as an electric dirt bike, ridden under the off-highway category of each classification naming this group. A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it, and each of those holds its own jurisdiction's license, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules.

restrictions.rule: Built by its manufacturer for off-highway use, not for the road
restrictions.citation: 49 U.S.C. §30102(a)(7); Illinois Vehicle Code §1-153.1; Utah Code §41-22-2

restrictions.rule: No limit on motor power or speed
restrictions.citation: Illinois Vehicle Code §1-153.1; Utah Code §41-22-2; Wisconsin Statutes §23.335(1)(q)

restrictions.rule: Kept off public roads except where its jurisdiction allows it
restrictions.citation: Ohio Revised Code §4519.40; Revised Code of Washington §46.09.450

evc/us/ak/electric-bicycle.name: Electric Bicycle
evc/us/ak/electric-bicycle.description: Alaska's statutes have no electric bicycle category, so on public roads one is a motor-driven cycle. The term is defined only for state parks: a bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes, the first under 500 watts.

restrictions.rule: In state parks, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph with a motor under 500 watts, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph

On public roads it isn't a bicycle, which Alaska defines as propelled only by human power, but a self-propelled motor vehicle licensed as a motor-driven cycle: the rider needs a driver's license, or at 14 or 15 an M2 permit
The DMV doesn't register e-bikes
In state parks, any class may ride roads open to cars or motorcycles and trails open to off-road vehicles

In state parks, only Class 1 may ride trails open to bicycles, including campground, picnic-area and paved trails, unless a trail is posted closed; a fat-tire Class 1 may ride wherever fat-tire bicycles may
A state park director may temporarily close a trail or area to e-bikes to protect the land, reduce user conflicts or for safety

evc/us/ca/electric-bicycle.name: Electric Bicycle
evc/us/ca/electric-bicycle.description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph with a speedometer.

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals and an electric motor that does not exceed 750 watts
A Class 1 or Class 3 motor can't propel it on its own past a 3.7 mph start assist or walk mode; Class 1 and Class 2 stop assisting at 20 mph, Class 3 at 28 mph, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer

Not an electric bicycle, and can't be sold, advertised or labeled as one, if its maker intends it to be modifiable so the motor alone can exceed 20 mph or the motor 750 watts, once it's modified so, or once its pedals are removed
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §312.5, as amended by SB 1271 (2024)

restrictions.rule: Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; it may be modified only if it still meets the definition and its label is replaced to match
No one may sell a product or device that changes an electric bicycle's speed so it no longer meets the definition
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §24016, as amended by AB 545 (2025)

restrictions.rule: No one may sell an app that changes an electric bicycle's speed so it no longer meets the definition
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §24016, as amended by AB 545 (2025)

restrictions.rule: Must meet the CPSC's bicycle requirements, and its motor must cut out when the brakes are applied or a switch is released
May only be sold with a battery tested by an accredited laboratory and marked with that laboratory's name or logo
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration, license plate or insurance

Riders under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet; on a Class 3, every rider and passenger must wear one; a minor's helmet ticket is excused by proof of a helmet and completion of an e-bike safety course, such as the CHP's
Riders must be 16 or older to ride a Class 3
A Class 3 can't be sold to anyone under 16
Must show a red reflector, or a solid or flashing red light with a built-in reflector, on the rear at all times, not only after dark
Ridden wherever bicycles may go, though a local authority may ban any class from an equestrian, hiking or recreational trail it manages, and State Parks from any bicycle path or trail
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §21207.5, as amended by AB 1909 (2022)

restrictions.rule: No class, Class 3 included, is barred from bike paths, bikeways or bike lanes
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §21207.5, as amended by AB 1909 (2022)

restrictions.rule: No city or county may require it to be licensed
A 10 mph prima facie speed limit on sidewalks, and a local authority may set a 10, 15 or 20 mph limit on a bike path or multiuse trail
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §§21214.8, 22352.1, added by AB 2346 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Anything with a motor over 750 watts, that can exceed 20 mph on the motor alone or get assistance past 28 mph, that its maker intends to be modifiable to, or that lacks operable pedals isn't an electric bicycle and can't be sold, advertised or labeled as one
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §312.5, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Sold with a written disclosure of its class, top speed, continuous and peak wattage, and the age, helmet and other laws for riding it, and a notice that modifying it to go faster than the law allows is illegal and can make it need a motorcycle license endorsement, registration and insurance
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §28170, added by AB 2346 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Every new Class 2 must have a speedometer, and every new electric bicycle front and rear lamps
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §28172, added by AB 2346 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Cities in San Mateo County may bar riders under 12 from Class 1 and Class 2 electric bicycles
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §21214.9, added by AB 2595 (2026)

evc/us/ca/moped.name: Moped
evc/us/ca/moped.description: A moped or motorized bicycle: two or three wheels, a motor under 4 gross brake horsepower (3,000 W), and a top speed of 30 mph on level ground.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels and an automatic transmission; one powered solely by electricity needs no pedals
Two or three wheels; pedals are optional
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §406, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Its motor produces less than 4 gross brake horsepower (3,000 W)
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §406, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground
Built for highway use: meets federal motor vehicle safety standards, with a 17-digit VIN and a safety certification label
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §406, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders need a driver's license with an M1 or M2 motorcycle endorsement, so must be 16 or older
Riders must wear a motorcycle helmet
Registered with the DMV and carries a moped plate; registering it doesn't require insurance
Barred from any freeway or expressway where Caltrans or the local authority posts a prohibition
Kept off bike paths and trails unless they run beside a roadway or a local ordinance allows it
A vehicle, not property: it can be towed or impounded

A peace officer may remove it when its rider isn't licensed to ride it and its motor alone can propel it faster than 20 mph; it's released after at least 48 hours, once the removal and storage costs are paid
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §22651.08, added by AB 875 (2025)

restrictions.rule: Its maker, importer or seller must warn buyers in every ad, online and social media included, that it's a motor vehicle subject to the helmet, registration, license and insurance laws that apply on a highway, and that their insurance may not cover it; buyers get the warning on its own sheet, and online must acknowledge it before buying
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §28191, added by SB 1167 (2026)

evc/us/ca/motor-driven-cycle.name: Motor-Driven Cycle
evc/us/ca/motor-driven-cycle.description: A light electric motorcycle: its motor produces 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less, the electric counterpart of a motorcycle under 150 cc.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle: a seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less; one under 3,000 W is a motor-driven cycle rather than a moped when it can go faster than 30 mph
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §405, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: The line is drawn only by an engine under 150 cc, which an electric motor doesn't have
Built for highway use: meets federal motor vehicle safety standards, with a 17-digit VIN and a safety certification label
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §405, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Riders need a driver's license with an M1 motorcycle endorsement
Riders must wear a motorcycle helmet
Registered and plated with the DMV, and must carry liability insurance
Barred from any freeway or expressway where Caltrans or the local authority posts a prohibition
Kept out of bike lanes except to park, enter or leave the road, or prepare to turn, and off any trail or bike path posted against unauthorized motor vehicles
A vehicle, not property: it can be towed or impounded

A peace officer may remove it when its rider isn't licensed to ride it and its motor alone can propel it faster than 20 mph; it's released after at least 48 hours, once the removal and storage costs are paid
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §22651.08, added by AB 875 (2025)

restrictions.rule: Its maker, importer or seller must warn buyers in every ad, online and social media included, that it's a motor vehicle subject to the helmet, registration, license and insurance laws that apply on a highway, and that their insurance may not cover it; buyers get the warning on its own sheet, and online must acknowledge it before buying
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §28191, added by SB 1167 (2026)

evc/us/ca/motorcycle.name: Motorcycle
evc/us/ca/motorcycle.description: A road-registered electric motorcycle: its motor produces more than 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W), above what a motor-driven cycle may.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces more than 5 gross brake horsepower (3,750 W)
One designed primarily for off-highway use, with two wheels, a straddle seat and no pedals, is an off-highway electric motorcycle instead
Riders need a driver's license with an M1 motorcycle endorsement
Riders must wear a motorcycle helmet
Registered and plated with the DMV, and must carry liability insurance
Allowed on freeways
Kept out of bike lanes except to park, enter or leave the road, or prepare to turn, and off any trail or bike path posted against unauthorized motor vehicles
A vehicle, not property: it can be towed or impounded

A peace officer may remove it when its rider isn't licensed to ride it and its motor alone can propel it faster than 20 mph; it's released after at least 48 hours, once the removal and storage costs are paid
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §22651.08, added by AB 875 (2025)

evc/us/ca/off-highway-electric-motorcycl.name: Off-Highway Electric Motorcycle
evc/us/ca/off-highway-electric-motorcycl.description: An electric motorcycle only permitted in designated OHV areas or on private property; never on streets, sidewalks, bike lanes, bike paths or highways. Can't be registered or converted for street use. No limit on power or speed.

restrictions.rule: Designed by the manufacturer primarily for off-highway use, with two wheels, handlebars, a straddle seat and no pedals from the manufacturer
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §436.1, added by SB 586 (2025)

restrictions.rule: No limit on motor power or speed
Not an electric bicycle or moped, whatever its power, and can't be sold or labeled as an electric bicycle; adding pedals doesn't make it one
Identified with a California OHV Green Sticker from the DMV to ride on public lands, or on private land open to the public
Ridden only in designated OHV areas or on private property; never on highways, streets, sidewalks, bike lanes or bike paths
Can't be registered or converted for street use
No driver's license needed off the highway; riding it on a highway is unregistered, unlicensed operation

Its maker, importer or seller must warn buyers in every ad, online and social media included, that it's a motor vehicle subject to the helmet, registration, license and insurance laws that apply on a highway, and that their insurance may not cover it; buyers get the warning on its own sheet, and online must acknowledge it before buying
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §28191, added by SB 1167 (2026)

restrictions.rule: Its makers are licensed as vehicle manufacturers and the shops selling it new as new motor vehicle dealers
restrictions.citation: California Vehicle Code §§426, 672, as amended by SB 1167 (2026)

evc/us/ca/off-highway-motor-vehicle.name: Off-Highway Motor Vehicle
evc/us/ca/off-highway-motor-vehicle.description: A motor vehicle used only off the highway and not registered for it, such as an electric ATV or off-road quad.

restrictions.rule: Not registered for highway use, so it can't be ridden on a highway, street, sidewalk, bike lane or bike path
Ridden only in designated OHV areas, on public lands open to off-highway vehicles, or on private property
Identified with a California OHV Green Sticker from the DMV to ride on public lands, or on private land open to the public; not needed on private land the owner controls

One that is an all-terrain vehicle (a single seat the operator straddles, three or more low-pressure tires, 50 inches or narrower and 900 lb or lighter) also needs: a motorcycle helmet on everyone aboard, a safety certificate, training course or certified adult's supervision for a rider under 18, a parent or authorized adult supervising a rider under 14, and no passenger unless it's built for one

evc/us/class-1.name: Class 1
evc/us/class-1.description: A pedal-assist electric bicycle: the motor helps only while the rider pedals, and stops helping at 20 mph. Every class is also a federal low-speed electric bicycle (evc/us/low-speed-electric-bicycle).

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and a motor of less than 750 watts
No throttle: the motor assists only while the rider is pedaling
The motor stops assisting at 20 mph, and disengages when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, bike lanes and bicycle or multi-use paths
A local authority may ban it from a bicycle or multi-use path only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
Treated as a bicycle, not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance

evc/us/class-2.name: Class 2
evc/us/class-2.description: A throttle electric bicycle: the motor can propel it without pedaling, and stops helping at 20 mph, by throttle or by pedal assist. Every class is also a federal low-speed electric bicycle (evc/us/low-speed-electric-bicycle).

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and a motor of less than 750 watts
The motor may propel it on its own, with a throttle, but can't assist at all at 20 mph or faster
The motor disengages when the brakes are applied
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, bike lanes and bicycle or multi-use paths
A local authority may ban it from a bicycle or multi-use path only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
Treated as a bicycle, not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance

evc/us/class-3.name: Class 3
evc/us/class-3.description: A speed pedal-assist electric bicycle: the motor helps only while the rider pedals, and stops helping at 28 mph. Every class is also a federal low-speed electric bicycle (evc/us/low-speed-electric-bicycle).

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and a motor of less than 750 watts
No throttle: the motor assists only while the rider is pedaling
The motor stops assisting at 28 mph, and disengages when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Riders and passengers must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements
A local authority may ban it from any bicycle or multi-use path, with no hearing needed
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
Treated as a bicycle, not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance

evc/us/co/electric-bicycle.name: Electrical Assisted Bicycle
evc/us/co/electric-bicycle.description: A vehicle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 and Class 3 assist only while the rider pedals, cutting out at 20 and 28 mph; Class 2 may assist without pedaling, to 20 mph
Class 1 and 3 need a cutoff that can't be bypassed, stopping the motor when the rider stops pedaling; a Class 2 motor stops when the brakes are applied
A vehicle modified out of every class, or built to be easily switched out of one by a button, setting or app, is not an electrical assisted bicycle
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-1-102(28.5), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: One whose motor exceeds 750 W, or that is modified out of its class, is a low-power scooter while its motor is 4,476 W or less with no manual clutch, needing a driver's license, registration and insurance, and a motorcycle past that, needing a motorcycle endorsement; one built for off-road use is an off-highway vehicle
A multiple-mode e-bike that can switch between classes must meet the rules of each class it can run as
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: A multiple-mode e-bike's label must name each class it can run as
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Carries a permanent label, in Arial at least 9-point, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage, and must not be modified to change its speed or motor engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Breaking the equipment, label or modification rules is a class B traffic infraction
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221(11), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Sellers must tell the buyer its motor wattage, top speed and class, and for one that can run as Class 3, that riding a Class 3 under 16 is unlawful in Colorado
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221(13), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: A vehicle that isn't an e-bike can't be sold, in a store or online, labeled as a Class 1, 2, 3 or multiple-mode e-bike or represented as one
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221(12), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Advertising or selling a vehicle that isn't an e-bike with the words e-bike, electric bike or similar takes a written disclosure, in the store and on its website and social media marketing, that it isn't an e-bike under state law but a motor vehicle subject to motor vehicle laws on public roads and lands, which insurance may not cover
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221(12), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Selling a vehicle labeled or represented as an e-bike that isn't one, or without that disclosure, is a deceptive trade practice under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §§42-4-221(12)(c), 6-1-105(1)(llll), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Its lithium-ion battery must be certified by an accredited lab to a UL 2849 or EN 15194 battery standard
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class 3 riders and passengers under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer
Class 1 and Class 2 may ride bike and pedestrian paths where bicycles are allowed, but a local authority may ban them from its paths
Class 3 is kept off bike and pedestrian paths unless the path is within a street or highway or the local authority allows it
On a sidewalk it yields to pedestrians, and local ordinances or signs may ban it there
In state parks, Class 1 and 2 may ride roads, bike lanes and trails open to bicycles
In state wildlife areas, e-bikes are limited to roads and camping or parking areas open to motor vehicles
Its rider has the same rights and duties as a bicyclist, and it is not a motor vehicle: no registration or driver's license

evc/us/in/electric-bicycle.name: Electric Bicycle
evc/us/in/electric-bicycle.description: A bicycle with operable pedals and an electric motor with a power output of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 and Class 3 pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class 2 throttle-assisted up to 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle with operable pedals and a motor with a power output of no more than 750 watts
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class 2 can be throttle-propelled up to 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph

One past these limits, with a motor over 750 watts or assisting past its class speed, isn't an electric bicycle but a motor vehicle: a motor driven cycle or motorcycle, registered with the BMV, when it meets federal motor vehicle safety standards, and otherwise an off-road vehicle kept off public roads
The motor must disengage or stop assisting when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; anyone who modifies its speed or motor engagement must update the label
Class 3 riders must be 15 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class 3 riders and passengers under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards
Regulated as a bicycle, with a bicycle rider's rights and duties, and may be ridden wherever bicycles may
Class 1 and Class 2 may use bicycle and multipurpose paths open to bicycles unless a statute, rule or local ordinance says otherwise
Class 3 is kept off bicycle and multipurpose paths unless the path runs within or beside a highway or the local authority or state agency in charge allows it
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the local authority or state agency that manages it decides which classes are allowed
On DNR properties all classes may use roads, Class 1 and Class 2 may use paved and gravel trails, and only Class 1 may use natural-surface trails open to bicycles
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, title, registration or insurance, and exempt from off-road vehicle rules

evc/us/nc/electric-bicycle.name: Electric Assisted Bicycle
evc/us/nc/electric-bicycle.description: A bicycle with two or three wheels, a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts. From December 1, 2026 it falls in one of three classes: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph; until then its motor alone may not push it past 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts
Its top speed on motor power alone on level ground is 20 mph
Class 1 assists only while the rider is pedaling and class 2 can propel it without pedaling, both to 20 mph; class 3 assists only while pedaling, to 28 mph
restrictions.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-4.01(7a), as amended by Session Law 2026-46

restrictions.rule: The helmet law for bicycle riders and passengers under 16, a $10 infraction for the parent, defines a bicycle as human-powered and doesn't name electric assisted bicycles, so it's unsettled whether it covers them
Riders and passengers under 18 on a class 3 must wear a helmet meeting federal safety standards
restrictions.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-171.3, enacted by Session Law 2026-46

restrictions.rule: No statewide minimum age, before or after the 2026 classes; the minimum of 16 is a moped's
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance
The rider has the duties of a vehicle driver under the traffic laws

It may be ridden on all roadways, bicycle lanes and multiuse paths, except where a city or county restricts it, or the Department of Natural and Cultural Resources does in state parks and historic sites
restrictions.citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-171.3, enacted by Session Law 2026-46

restrictions.rule: Cities and counties may restrict classes and set speed limits on multiuse paths and sidewalks, and may require helmets for riders and passengers under 18 on class 1 and class 2
No class label, anti-tampering or sales disclosure rule in state law, before or after the 2026 classes

One past these limits with pedals that tops out at 20 mph is a motor-driven bicycle, under motorcycle rules; one with no external shifter that tops out at 30 mph is a moped, which needs registration, insurance, a helmet and a rider 16 or older; any other is a motorcycle

evc/us/nj/dirt-bike.name: Dirt Bike
evc/us/nj/dirt-bike.description: A two-wheeled motorcycle designed and manufactured for off-road use only that doesn't meet federal motor vehicle safety standards or EPA on-road emissions standards, such as an off-road e-moto.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels, designed and manufactured for off-road use only, and not compliant with federal motor vehicle safety standards or EPA on-road emissions standards
Registered with the Motor Vehicle Commission to ride on public lands or waters or to cross a public highway
The rider must carry proof of liability insurance and current registration
Riders must be 14 or older on public lands or waters or crossing a public highway
Riders under 18 must complete an approved safety course and carry the certificate while riding
For off-road use only

Never ridden on a limited-access highway or its right-of-way; on another public street only to cross it directly, registered, after a full stop, or alongside it to reach where it's ridden when it can't be unloaded closer

Ridden on a public street, highway or right-of-way, it's impounded for at least 7 days, released on proof of registration and insurance and a $500 fee plus towing and storage; a repeat offense means at least 14 days and $750, and one unclaimed after 30 days may be auctioned
A municipality may by ordinance make one ridden on a public street or highway contraband, forfeited and possibly destroyed

Ridden on public lands against the off-road vehicle law, it may be impounded for at least 48 hours with a $500 fee, 96 hours and $750 for a second offense, and forfeited and auctioned, with a $1,000 fee, for a third
Banned from all New Jersey state parks and forests

evc/us/nj/electric-bicycle.name: Low-Speed Electric Bicycle
evc/us/nj/electric-bicycle.description: A two-wheeled bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor that helps only while the rider pedals and stops helping at 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels and fully operable pedals; the motor assists only while the rider is pedaling and stops assisting at 20 mph
restrictions.citation: N.J.S.A. 39:1-1, as amended by P.L.2025, c.285

restrictions.rule: The definition sets no motor wattage limit

An e-bike with a throttle, or with pedal assist past 20 mph up to 28 mph, is a motorized bicycle instead: it also needs a license and registration, must carry liability insurance, its rider must wear a helmet at any age, and it is barred from roads posted over 50 mph
One with pedals and a motor over 750 watts that can exceed 28 mph is an electric motorized bicycle, which the law counts as a motorcycle
Riders must be 15 or older
Riders need a driver's license or a motorized bicycle (e-bike) license from the Motor Vehicle Commission, which takes a knowledge test and a road test; 15- and 16-year-olds need the e-bike license
Registered with the Motor Vehicle Commission, with its two plate stickers displayed on the front fork
Its seller must make the Motor Vehicle Commission's registration forms available to the buyer
No insurance required
Riders under 17 must wear a bicycle helmet
Ridden on streets, highways and bicycle paths; a county or municipality may ban it from bicycle paths it controls
May be parked on a sidewalk if it doesn't block pedestrians
Kept off natural-surface trails designated non-motorized unless the local authority allows it
Must not be tampered with or modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement
Selling a kit that converts it into a motorized or electric motorized bicycle is prohibited
Not a motor vehicle; the laws that apply to bicycles otherwise apply to it
A bike-share rider 16 or older needs no license, and the rider doesn't register a shared e-bike

evc/us/nj/motorized-bicycle.name: Motorized Bicycle
evc/us/nj/motorized-bicycle.description: A pedal bicycle with an electric motor that assists while pedaling or runs on a throttle, up to 28 mph on a flat surface, or with a helper motor under 50 cc or rated at no more than 1.5 brake horsepower; the Motor Vehicle Commission calls it a moped.

restrictions.rule: A pedal bicycle: an electric motor that assists while the rider pedals or propels it on a throttle, with a top motor-powered speed of 28 mph on a flat surface; or a helper motor under 50 cc or rated at no more than 1.5 brake horsepower
A throttle e-bike, or a pedal-assist e-bike that keeps assisting past 20 mph, lands here rather than in the low-speed electric bicycle category
restrictions.citation: N.J.S.A. 39:1-1, as amended by P.L.2025, c.285

restrictions.rule: One with pedals, a motor capable of more than 750 watts and a top speed over 28 mph is an electric motorized bicycle, which the law counts as a motorcycle
Riders must be 15 or older; riders 15 and 16 need a moped (class F) license, and riders 17 and older need any driver's license or a moped license
The moped license takes a knowledge test and a riding demonstration
Registered with the Motor Vehicle Commission, with two plate stickers on the front fork
Its seller must make the Motor Vehicle Commission's registration forms available to the buyer
One not registrable before P.L.2025, c.285 had a grace period to register
The owner must carry liability insurance, and the rider must carry the license, registration and insurance card
Riders of any age must wear a protective helmet of a type the Motor Vehicle Commission approves
Carries only the operator
Barred from interstate highways, highways divided by a median, highways posted over 50 mph, and public land where the agency in charge prohibits it
Bicycle rules otherwise apply, and on a road the rider has the duties of a vehicle driver
Selling a kit that turns a low-speed electric bicycle into a motorized bicycle is prohibited

evc/us/ny/electric-bicycle.name: Bicycle With Electric Assist
evc/us/ny/electric-bicycle.description: A bicycle no more than 36 inches wide, with operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3, which may run on the motor alone to 25 mph and is allowed only in a city of a million or more people.

restrictions.rule: No more than 36 inches wide, with operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts
Class 1 assists only while the rider is pedaling and class 2 may be propelled by the motor alone; both stop assisting at 20 mph
Class 3 may be propelled by the motor alone and stops assisting at 25 mph; it may be ridden only in a city of a million or more people, which means New York City
Past these limits it isn't a bicycle with electric assist: with a seat and a top speed of 40 mph or less it's a limited use motorcycle, and faster a motorcycle, either of which must be registered
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Carries a label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Riders must be 16 or older
Class 3 riders must wear a helmet
Not registered with the DMV
State law allows it on roads with a posted speed limit of 30 mph or less and in bicycle lanes
Not ridden on a sidewalk unless a local law allows it; may be parked on one if it leaves pedestrians room to pass
Cities, towns and villages may further regulate when, where and how it's ridden, including speed limits, helmets and reflective gear
In New York City, capped at 15 mph
On public lands other than roads it may be ridden only where the agency in charge authorizes it

State parks allow class 1 and class 2 on boardwalks and paved or improved paths at up to 15 mph, and class 1 alone on natural-surface trails open to bicycles; class 3 is banned at every state park facility, and all classes from parkways
Breaking these rules carries a civil fine of up to $50

evc/us/pa/electric-bicycle.name: Pedalcycle With Electric Assist
evc/us/pa/electric-bicycle.description: A single category, not the three-class system: a pedalcycle of 100 pounds or less with operable pedals and an electric motor rated at no more than 750 watts that can't propel it past 20 mph on its own, legally a bicycle.

restrictions.rule: Weighs no more than 100 pounds, with two or three wheels more than 11 inches in diameter
restrictions.citation: Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes Title 75 §102, as amended by Act 154 of 2014

restrictions.rule: Operable pedals and an electric motor rated at no more than 750 watts
The motor alone can't propel it faster than 20 mph on a level surface; a throttle is allowed
No class system: Pennsylvania has not adopted the three-class model law
Riders must be 16 or older
Riders and passengers under 12 must wear a bicycle helmet, including a child in a bike seat or towed trailer
Carries only as many riders as it's designed for, though an adult may carry a child in an attached child seat or trailer
No driver's license, title, registration or insurance
Follows the same rules of the road as a bicycle; banned from freeways
May be ridden on sidewalks, yielding to pedestrians, except in a business district unless signs allow it or where a bike lane runs alongside

In state parks, allowed on roads and on trails open to bicycles, but must be pedaled, not run on throttle alone, on non-motorized trails; barred from natural areas and yellow- or orange-blazed hiking trails

In state forests, allowed on roads and on trails open to bicycles, but must be pedaled, not run on throttle alone, on non-motorized trails; barred from natural areas and yellow- or orange-blazed hiking trails
A parent may not knowingly let their child break these rules; a violation is a summary offense with a $10 fine
One with pedals and an automatic transmission that exceeds these limits but has a top design speed of 25 mph or less is a motorized pedalcycle, a motor vehicle that needs a Class C driver's license

evc/us/tx/electric-bicycle.name: Electric Bicycle
evc/us/tx/electric-bicycle.description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts, with a top assisted speed of 28 mph or less, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals and an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts, with a top assisted speed of 28 mph or less
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals, to a top assisted speed of 20 mph
Class 2 can be propelled by its motor without pedaling, to a top assisted speed of 20 mph
Class 3 assists only while the rider pedals, to a top assisted speed of more than 20 but less than 28 mph, and must be sold with a speedometer
May only be ridden if the motor disengages when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; anyone who changes its motor-powered speed or engagement must replace the label to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements
Class 3 riders must be 15 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one
No statewide helmet requirement
No driver's license, title or insurance, and it can't be registered for highway use
TxDOT and local authorities may not ban it from roads used mainly by motor vehicles, or from anywhere a regular bicycle may go, except natural-surface trails closed to motor vehicles
TxDOT and local authorities may ban bicycles, e-bikes included, from sidewalks and set speed limits on bicycle paths

evc/us/tx/off-highway-motorcycle.name: Off-Highway Motorcycle
evc/us/tx/off-highway-motorcycle.description: A motorcycle ridden for off-highway recreation, one of the off-highway vehicles that need a Texas Parks and Wildlife decal on public riding land, which is how an off-road electric dirt bike is ridden legally.

restrictions.rule: Counted as an off-highway vehicle under the state's off-highway trail program, which sets no limit on motor power or speed

Needs an annual off-highway vehicle decal from Texas Parks and Wildlife, at least $8 and valid September through August, to ride on public land or land developed with a department grant where off-highway riding is legal

The Transportation Code calls a seated two-wheeler with an electric motor that isn't designed for highway use and can't be titled a pocket bike or minimotorbike, and nothing in Texas's scooter law authorizes one on a road, street, bicycle path or sidewalk
The all-terrain vehicle rules, including their safety certificate, cover only vehicles on three or more tires

evc/eu/epac.name: Electrically Power Assisted Cycle (EPAC)
evc/eu/epac.description: The EU's e-bike: a pedal cycle whose auxiliary electric motor of no more than 250 W assists only while the rider pedals and cuts out by 25 km/h. Excluded from EU type approval, it needs no EU approval, licence or motor insurance, and is sold as machinery under the CE marking; member states set where and how it's ridden.

restrictions.rule: A pedal cycle with pedal assistance from an auxiliary electric motor
The motor's maximum continuous rated power, its maximum 30-minute power at the output shaft, is 250 W or less
The motor cuts out when the cyclist stops pedalling, and otherwise its output is progressively reduced and finally cut off before the cycle reaches 25 km/h
The Regulation makes no exception to the cut-out when pedalling stops, but the harmonised standard EN 15194 allows a start-up (walk) assistance mode that drives it without pedalling up to 6 km/h
Outside EU type approval, so it has no certificate of conformity, which an L-category vehicle needs to be sold or registered
No EU driving licence category covers it: the AM moped licence excludes vehicles with a maximum design speed of 25 km/h or less

Outside the Motor Insurance Directive's compulsory insurance, which covers only motor vehicles propelled exclusively by mechanical power with a maximum design speed over 25 km/h, or over 14 km/h when their net weight is over 25 kg; a member state may still require insurance for it under national law
restrictions.citation: Directive 2009/103/EC, Art. 1(1), as amended by Directive (EU) 2021/2118; Directive (EU) 2021/2118, recitals 4, 6

restrictions.rule: The Court of Justice held that a bicycle whose motor only assists pedalling isn't a vehicle under the Motor Insurance Directive, even with a boost to 20 km/h without pedalling that only muscular power can start
restrictions.citation: Judgment of 12 October 2023, KBC Verzekeringen, C-286/22

restrictions.rule: Machinery under the Machinery Directive, whose exclusion of type-approved two- and three-wheelers doesn't reach it: before sale the manufacturer must meet the Directive's essential health and safety requirements, draw up an EC declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking
Built to EN 15194:2017+A1:2023 it's presumed to meet those requirements, except on vibration, which the standard's listing excludes
restrictions.citation: Directive 2006/42/EC, Art. 7(2); Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1586, Annex I, item 495a

restrictions.rule: The Machinery Regulation replaces the Directive and covers e-bikes outside EU type approval, except for the risks of riding on public roads: the manufacturer must meet its essential health and safety requirements, draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking

evc/ca/nb/motorcycle.name: Motorcycle
evc/ca/nb/motorcycle.description: Any vehicle with a saddle for the rider, designed to travel on no more than three wheels, other than a tractor; a road-registered electric motorcycle is one. The motor driven cycle is split off only by a 50 cc engine displacement, and the licence endorsements only by engine size, with no electric equivalent.

restrictions.rule: A saddle for the rider and no more than three wheels on the ground; no power or speed limits
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 1

restrictions.rule: Riders need a licence endorsed valid for motorcycle (Class 6), after holding a motorcycle learner's licence for 12 months and passing a road test
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, ss. 78(2), 84.11(6); General Regulation, N.B. Reg. 83-42, s. 22

restrictions.rule: The learner's licence is available from age 16, after a licensed motorcycle training course and the written exams; a learner may not carry a passenger, tow, ride between sunset and sunrise or have any alcohol in their blood
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 84.11

restrictions.rule: Every rider and passenger must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting a listed standard
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 229; General Regulation, N.B. Reg. 83-42, s. 38

restrictions.rule: Both hands on the handlebars and both feet on the footrests, seated on the permanent seat; a passenger only if it's designed for one
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 199(1)

restrictions.rule: Needs a mirror on each side and a brake operable by hand or foot
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, ss. 233(2), 237(2)

restrictions.rule: Registered for $47 a year, and must carry motor vehicle liability insurance
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 17.1; General Regulation, N.B. Reg. 83-42, s. 5

restrictions.rule: Entitled to a full traffic lane, but may not pass in the same lane or ride abreast another motorcycle except to pass
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 199

restrictions.rule: One built for off-road use and not registered under the Motor Vehicle Act is an off-road vehicle instead
restrictions.citation: Off-Road Vehicle Act, SNB 1985, c O-1.5, s. 1

evc/ca/on/power-assisted-bicycle.name: Power-Assisted Bicycle
evc/ca/on/power-assisted-bicycle.description: A bicycle meeting the federal power-assisted bicycle definition, with motors totalling 500 W or less that stop assisting at 32 km/h, operable pedals and an unladen weight of no more than 120 kg; nothing in it excludes a scooter- or motorcycle-style body.

restrictions.rule: Meets the federal power-assisted bicycle definition and bears its manufacturer's label, with pedals that are operable at all times and can propel it on level ground by muscular power alone
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: Its definition still points to the federal one, though Canada repealed that in 2021
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: Its motors total 500 W or less and can't assist past 32 km/h
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1); Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Weighs no more than 120 kg unladen, with wheels at least 35 mm wide and 350 mm in diameter
The motor must stop propelling it when pedalling stops, the throttle is released or the brakes are applied, and the battery and motor must be securely fastened
Brakes on both wheels able to stop it from 30 km/h within 9 metres, and all electric terminals insulated and covered
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 64(2); O. Reg. 369/09, ss. 4, 5

restrictions.rule: Must not be ridden if modified to raise its power or speed past the federal limits; removing the pedals makes it a motor vehicle
restrictions.citation: O. Reg. 369/09, s. 6; Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: Riders must be 16 or older
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 38(1)

restrictions.rule: Every rider must wear a bicycle or motorcycle helmet
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 103.1(2)

restrictions.rule: No passenger unless it's designed to carry more than one person
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 178(2)

restrictions.rule: Not a motor vehicle: no driver's licence, registration, plates or insurance
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: Ridden under the rules of the road for cyclists, wherever bicycles are allowed
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: Not allowed on the 400-series highways, the Queen Elizabeth Way or the other controlled-access highways listed in Regulation 630
A municipality may ban it from its roads, sidewalks, bike paths, trails or bike lanes by by-law
A cargo e-bike over 55 kg with a motor of up to 1,000 W can instead run under the cargo power-assisted bicycle pilot, where a municipality allows it

The Safer Roads and Communities Act, 2024 repeals this definition and drops power-assisted bicycles from the Act's bicycle and motor vehicle definitions, on a day not yet named by proclamation, so regulations can replace it
restrictions.citation: Safer Roads and Communities Act, 2024, S.O. 2024, c. 21, s. 1

restrictions.rule: An April 2026 Ministry proposal (ERO 026-0422) would split e-bikes into pedal-assist and throttle classes and push scooter- and motorcycle-style ones into the motor vehicle classes; it isn't in force

evc/ca/on/limited-speed-motorcycle.name: Limited-Speed Motorcycle
evc/ca/on/limited-speed-motorcycle.description: A moped or motor scooter that can go faster than 32 km/h but no faster than 70 km/h; an electric one qualifies by carrying the federal compliance label that identifies it as a limited-speed motorcycle. Outside the rules naming it, it's a motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle able to exceed 32 km/h within 1.6 km of a standing start, with a top speed of 70 km/h or less, a seat at least 650 mm high, wheel rims at least 250 mm and a wheelbase of at least 1,016 mm
Qualifies with an engine of 50 cc or less, or, if built since September 1, 1988, with the manufacturer's federal compliance label identifying it as a limited-speed motorcycle (LSM/MVL)
No limit on motor wattage
Riders must be 16 or older with a class M licence
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 37(1); O. Reg. 340/94, s. 2(1)

restrictions.rule: Passing the road tests on one limits the licence to limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds (the L condition), and an M2-L rider may use only roads with a speed limit of 80 km/h or less
Must be registered and plated, and carry liability insurance
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 7(1); Compulsory Automobile Insurance Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.25, s. 2(1)

restrictions.rule: Every rider must wear a motorcycle helmet with the chin strap fastened
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 104(1)

restrictions.rule: Not allowed on the 400-series highways, the Queen Elizabeth Way or the other controlled-access highways listed in Regulation 630

evc/ca/nb/motor-driven-cycle.name: Motor Driven Cycle
evc/ca/nb/motor-driven-cycle.description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle on no more than three wheels and a motor of 50 cc or less, motor scooters and motorized bicycles included; the statute measures the motor only by displacement, so for an electric scooter or moped the working limits are the General Regulation's 50 km/h motor and 55 kg weight caps. New Brunswick has no e-bike category: its bicycle is human-powered only, so an e-bike is a motorized bicycle here.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels; the statutory limit is a motor of 50 cc or less, with no wattage equivalent
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 1

restrictions.rule: Weighs 55 kg or less, with wheel rims at least 25 cm in diameter, a seat 70 cm off the ground and an automatic transmission
Its motor can't propel it faster than 50 km/h
Needs one to three white headlamps and a red tail lamp visible from 150 m, and can't exceed 60 km/h at night unless its headlamp lights 100 m ahead
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, ss. 145, 209; General Regulation, N.B. Reg. 83-42, s. 46

restrictions.rule: The rider has the rights and duties of a motor vehicle driver
Riders need a licence for motor-driven cycles, available from age 14; Class 9 covers it, as do Classes 5 and 6
Every rider must wear a motorcycle helmet
No passengers, and no riding abreast another motor-driven cycle except to pass
Registered with one plate, for $33 a year, and must carry motor vehicle liability insurance
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 17.1; General Regulation, N.B. Reg. 83-42, ss. 5, 45

restrictions.rule: Can be banned from controlled-access roadways by the authority responsible for them
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Act, RSNB 1973, c M-17, s. 160

restrictions.rule: Bill 113 (royal assent June 10, 2022), which would let regulations bring other devices into the bicycle definition, comes into force only on proclamation, and hadn't been proclaimed as of the Act's June 12, 2026 consolidation

evc/us/nj/motorcycle.name: Motorcycle
evc/us/nj/motorcycle.description: Any motor-operated vehicle of the bicycle or tricycle type with a seat the rider sits astride or a platform to stand on, including motor bikes and electric motorized bicycles, other than a motorized bicycle, low-speed electric bicycle or low-speed electric scooter. An electric two-wheeler without pedals, or a pedaled one past the motorized bicycle limits, is one.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle the rider sits astride, or a platform the rider stands on, on two or three wheels
Takes in motor bikes, bicycles with a motor attached and electric motorized bicycles; excludes motorized bicycles, low-speed electric bicycles and low-speed electric scooters
restrictions.citation: N.J.S.A. 39:1-1, as amended by P.L.2025, c.285

restrictions.rule: An electric two-wheeler without pedals, a seated e-moped included, can't be a motorized bicycle, which must be a pedal bicycle, or a low-speed electric scooter, which is stood on and stays under 19 mph, so it is a motorcycle at any power or speed; New Jersey has no separate motor-driven cycle class
Riders need a motorcycle endorsement on a driver's license or a separate motorcycle license; applicants must be 17 or older, with parental consent under 18
Riders under 18 must complete the Basic Rider Course
Riders and passengers must wear a securely fitted, approved protective helmet with a chin strap and reflectorization on both sides
Titled, registered and insured with the Motor Vehicle Commission
No state safety inspection

53.name: 7.7 x 2.8in
53.description: 7.7 x 2.8in (196 x 71) PU wheel, Vanpowers VanSwift mobility scooter (Rare)

93.name: 8in
93.description: 8in (200 x 50, ETRTO 47-93) smaller e-scooters and hoverboards (Uncommon)

102.name: 7 x 1.5in
102.description: 7 x 1.5in (178 x 38) solid wheel, NIU KQi Youth kids' e-scooter rear (Rare)

110.name: 6.5in
110.description: 6.5in solid tire, Hiboy S2 Lite and hoverboard-style scooters (Uncommon)

115.name: 7.5 x 1.5in
115.description: 7.5 x 1.5in (191 x 38) solid wheel, NIU KQi Youth kids' e-scooter front (Rare)

134.name: 8.5in
134.description: 8.5in (8 1/2 x 2, ISO 50-134) Xiaomi M365/Pro and most 8.5in e-scooters (Common)

145.name: 9in
145.description: 9in (9 x 2) Hiboy S2R Plus and other 9in e-scooters (Uncommon)

152.name: 10in
152.description: 10in (10 x 2, 54-152) Ninebot ES/Max and many 10in e-scooters (Common)

155.name: 9.5in
155.description: 9.5in (9.5 x 2.5-6.1) NIU KQi3, KQi 100 and KQi Air e-scooters (Uncommon)

165.name: 11in
165.description: 11in (90/65-6.5; Ninebot Max 10in uses 60/70-6.5) Dualtron, Ninebot Max e-scooters (Uncommon)

175.name: 10in (6.9in rim)
175.description: 10in (60/65-6.9) Segway Ninebot Max G2, E2 Pro, E3, F3 e-scooters (Uncommon)

191.name: 11in (7.5in rim)
191.description: 11in (7.5in rim) Segway GT3, Max G3 e-scooters (Uncommon)

356.name: 14in moto
